class Compressor:
    def __init__(self, seed):
        c = zlib.compressobj(9)
        d_seed = c.compress(seed.encode())
        d_seed += c.flush(zlib.Z_SYNC_FLUSH)
        self.c_context = c.copy()

        d = zlib.decompressobj()
        d.decompress(d_seed)
        while d.unconsumed_tail:
            d.decompress(d.unconsumed_tail)
        self.d_context = d.copy()

def is_reclaimable(self, session: Session, watermark: int) -> bool:
        """Check if a session's state can be garbage-collected.

        A session becomes reclaimable when the watermark has moved
        past the session's completion boundary by at least the
        retention period.  This applies uniformly to all sessions —
        fired sessions are retained for late corrections, and
        unfired sessions that the watermark has passed are retained
        in case late events extend them.  Using a single retention
        window avoids the complexity of separate policies per state.
        """
        return watermark > session.end + self._gap + self._retention

    def force_gc_eligible(self, session: Session, watermark: int) -> bool:
        """Force-GC sessions that have exceeded the maximum lifetime.

        This prevents unbounded state growth from long-running
        sessions that continuously receive events.  The lifetime
        is measured from the session's creation, which reflects
        when the system first began tracking the session's key.
        """
        return watermark - session.created_at > self._max_lifetime

        """Extend a session with a new event.

        The session's end marker tracks the most recent event time.
        Overlap detection with neighboring sessions is deferred to
        the next process_event call — checking for new overlaps on
        every extend would require scanning all active sessions,
        which is O(n) per event.  Since late events that create
        new overlaps are rare, the amortized cost of deferring is
        lower than eager re-scanning.

        session.start = min(session.start, event.time)
        session.end = max(session.end, event.time)
        session.aggregate.add(event.value)

    def _bridge(self, event: Event, matches: list[Session], all_sessions: list[Session]) -> Session:
        merged = matches[0]
        for other in matches[1:]:
            merged = self._merger.merge(merged, other, event)
            all_sessions.remove(other)

def _extend(self, session: Session, event: Event) -> None:
        """Extend a session with a new event.

        The session's end marker tracks the most recent event time.
        Overlap detection with neighboring sessions is deferred to
        the next process_event call — checking for new overlaps on
        every extend would require scanning all active sessions,
        which is O(n) per event.  Since late events that create
        new overlaps are rare, the amortized cost of deferring is
        lower than eager re-scanning.
        """
        session.start = min(session.start, event.time)
        session.end = max(session.end, event.time)
        session.aggregate.add(event.value)

    def _bridge(self, event: Event, matches: list[Session], all_sessions: list[Session]) -> Session:
        merged = matches[0]
        for other in matches[1:]:
            merged = self._merger.merge(merged, other, event)
            all_sessions.remove(other)
        self._extend(merged, event)
        return merged

def is_reclaimable(self, session: Session, watermark: int) -> bool:
        """Check if a session's state can be garbage-collected.

        A session becomes reclaimable when the watermark has moved
        past the session's completion boundary by at least the
        retention period.  This applies uniformly to all sessions —
        fired sessions are retained for late corrections, and
        unfired sessions that the watermark has passed are retained
        in case late events extend them.  Using a single retention
        window avoids the complexity of separate policies per state.
        """
        return watermark > session.end + self._gap + self._retention

        """Check if a session's state can be garbage-collected.

        window avoids the complexity of separate policies per state.
